cases.assertion: Ordered original fragments preserve internal whitespace, trim outer whitespace, omit separators and empty fragments, accept a final statement without a semicolon, and leave input unchanged.
Semicolons and doubled quotes inside standard strings and identifiers do not split; standard-conforming backslashes do not escape closing quotes; UTF-8 and comment-looking text are preserved.
Both E and e strings retain escaped quotes, doubled quotes, semicolons and even backslash runs without corrupting statement boundaries.
An E/e embedded in an identifier does not enable backslash escaping; an E prefix after an opening parenthesis does.
Untagged and valid ASCII tagged dollar quotes preserve bodies with semicolons and apparent comments or quotes; closing tags must match case exactly.
Dollar sequences within unquoted identifiers and positional parameters are ordinary text; invalid ASCII tag shapes do not open quotes, while valid tags at token boundaries do.
Nested block comments suppress all internal boundaries and quote-like text; apparent comments inside strings or identifiers do not independently open regions.
Line comments end at CR, LF or CRLF, permit EOF, ignore quote and block-comment openers, and remain preserved when attached to a statement.
Unterminated standard strings, E/e strings, identifiers, dollar quotes and nested block comments raise ValueError starting with Unterminated SQL, including after an earlier complete statement.
Empty and comment-only fragments are discarded while original leading and trailing comments on executable statements remain intact.

Real PostgreSQL executes UTF-8 quoted semicolons, quoted identifiers, a tagged function body, an untagged DO body and nested comments. Every expected original statement is a separate execute call; the file receives one ledger entry and bootstrap plus file commits.

A real SQL error rolls back earlier DML and DDL within its file and omits its ledger row, preserves a prior committed file, stops later files, and permits successful retry after correcting only the failed file.
Malformed trailing string, identifier, dollar quote or block comment prevents even a valid preceding statement from being sent to PostgreSQL; prior committed migration and ledger persist.
Rerun skips an applied filename even after its contents become lexically invalid; data and complete ledger rows remain identical and only bootstrap is committed.
Empty and comment-only files each receive one ledger row and one explicit file commit, no executable comment statements, and no additional rows or file commits on replay.
Only immediate .sql files execute in filename order despite reverse creation order; nested SQL and non-SQL files are ignored, UTF-8 values are correct, and the run emits console summary output.

The public runner retains its sole optional migrations_dir parameter with default None, accepts keyword invocation and returns None; an empty directory bootstraps an empty isolated ledger with one explicit commit.

limitations: No candidate or old implementation is executed during design; only static syntax and design-to-function matching are checked before freeze.

Database tests depend on the unchanged test_database fixture and provisioned PostgreSQL. They use a unique schema with no public search_path fallback and verify the fixture public ledger is unchanged.
The default filesystem migration directory and exact legacy summary wording are not asserted; explicit directory discovery, the public default parameter and presence of console output are covered.
The unchanged project suite is left to the controller. COPY input, transaction-control statements, psql commands, non-ASCII dollar tags, concurrency and checksum tracking are outside the contract.
